headline: Adani Group agrees to acquire Europe's Evos B.V. for €2.56 billion
hook: Port giant enters continental liquid storage
summary: Adani Group has entered an agreement to acquire Evos B.V., Europe's second-largest liquid storage operator, for €2.56 billion. The transaction expands Adani's infrastructure footprint into the European market, adding specialized liquid bulk storage capabilities to its global logistics portfolio. For Indian retail investors, this cross-border acquisition demonstrates the group's continued overseas expansion strategy funded through international debt and internal accruals.
whats_next: Regulatory approvals and financial closure of the €2.56bn deal
why_it_matters: Adani expands European logistics footprint via major acquisition
winners_losers: Adani Group gains / European competitors challenged

headline: Adani Ports to acquire Dutch terminal operator Evos for €1.18 billion
hook: Adani Ports expands European terminal footprint
summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) has entered into an agreement to acquire the Dutch liquid storage company Evos for €1.18 billion. Evos operates a network of eight terminals across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Spain, with a total storage capacity of 6.9 million cubic meters. This acquisition marks a significant expansion of Adani's logistics infrastructure into the European market. The deal is expected to strengthen the company's global terminal network and liquid storage capabilities.
why_it_matters: Global expansion strengthens Adani Ports' long-term revenue diversification.
winners_losers: Adani Ports gains / European competitors face pressure

headline: Adani Ports acquires European liquid storage firm Evos for €2.56 billion
hook: Europe expansion adds 6.3m cubic metres capacity
summary: Adani Ports has signed an agreement to acquire 100% of Netherlands-based Evos B.V. at an enterprise value of €2.56 billion. The transaction expands the company's global footprint to 28 ports and terminals across 10 countries, adding 6.3 million cubic metres of liquid storage capacity and 37 MMT of annual throughput. Evos reported a 56% EBITDA margin in calendar year 2025, bolstering the acquirer's international revenue mix. Indian retail investors holding Adani Ports should note this large cross-border expansion diversifies earnings outside domestic operations.
whats_next: Regulatory approvals and deal closure timeline
why_it_matters: Global footprint expands with large European liquid storage acquisition
winners_losers: Adani Ports gains / global peers face competition
